findings: The archive is two datasets in one. Before October 2026, 87% of incidents come from the CISA list. In October 2026, 142 of 160 do not, so that month’s spike reflects wider coverage, not a surge in attacks.
Coverage of the CISA list is complete for 2024 and 2025 but not for the other years: 78% of 2023 and 66% of 2026. Counting those incidents would wrongly suggest a fall in 2026.
Severity labels shifted too: 49% of CISA-listed incidents from 2025 are marked critical, against 7% from 2026.
12 of the 31 incidents tagged AI started in October 2026. That is too recent, and too affected by the coverage change, to call a trend.
83% of incidents have a fix. 14 are unpatched and 72 are partly patched.
